subject.title: fix(claws): harden add and remove lifecycle

question: Should consented Claw removal remain the sole caller allowed to bypass the config-size-drop guard, with ordinary agent deletion continuing to fail closed?
rationale: This is an intentional authorization and integrity-boundary exception rather than a mechanical refactor; the PR body asserts approval, but the protected maintainer label and contributor association require independently confirmed owner intent before merge.

options.title: Confirm the narrow exception
options.body: Approve the exception only for provenance-checked, consented Claw removal and require tests proving ordinary agent deletion still retains the guard.

options.title: Keep the generic guard absolute
options.body: Remove the bypass and redesign the Claw removal flow so it satisfies the existing config-size protection without a special exception.

recommendation.title: Confirm the narrow exception
recommendation.body: Approve the exception only for provenance-checked, consented Claw removal and require tests proving ordinary agent deletion still retains the guard.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest supplied history connection to the experimental Claws lifecycle and authored the prior merged implementation, though an independently confirmed repository owner should make the final boundary decision.
